current_law_statement: Codified La. R.S. 44:32 opened at legis.la.gov on 2026-08-19; amendment line ends with Acts 2024, No. 411 (HB 113 — added (C)(2)(b), student media at postsecondary institutions; not municipal). Fee text for local bodies last changed by Acts 2023, No. 247 (SB 213, eff. Aug. 1, 2023: 'transmission of electronic copies' + mandatory posted reasonable fee schedule). 44:35 last amended Acts 2024, No. 493 (eff. June 5, 2024). 2025 and 2026 Regular Sessions reviewed for the fee sections: no enacted change found; 2026 RS SB 493 (Reese — 20 free pages, 5c/page cap, $10 electronic cap, ban on staff-time charges, website posting) was withdrawn from the Senate files 4/22/2026 and is NOT law. State-agency delegation followed to LAC 4:I.301 (DOA Office of the State Register compilation, opened; last amended LR 12:229, Apr. 1986). Guidance-vs-law gap: the Louisiana DOJ 2023 CLE outline and AG opinions (17-0056, 15-0056, 17-0044) supply the no-labor-charge and reasonable-fee content the statute states only by omission; the Legislative Auditor FAQ (rev. 3/10/2022) predates Act 247 and does not mention the posted-schedule duty. AG Op. 96-270 (urging local bodies to adopt the state schedule) could not be opened.

resolutions.source_language: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, which may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)
resolutions.notes: Standard term: 'reasonable fees for making copies'. No statutory number for non-state-agency custodians (municipalities); the custodian who elects to charge must adopt and post a reasonable fee schedule (LA-0022). AG Op. 15-0056 (LA-9010): a reasonable fee 'does include, at a minimum, the actual costs for making the copies' and is not to recoup generation cost. State-agency regime (NOT binding on cities): LAC 4:I.301.B sets a $0.25/page minimum for paper copies up to 8.5x14 (LA-9002) — usable only as guidance/reference. 2026 RS SB 493 (20 free pages, 5c/page cap) was withdrawn 4/22/2026 and is not law.

resolutions.source_language: No provision of the Public Records Law directly authorizes such a charge to the requester. We must therefore return to La. R.S. 44:32(C)(3) and the default rule that a requester may not be charged a fee in connection with a request to examine public records, nor for a custodian's pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records. See La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0173, supra. We are therefore of the opinion that a custodian may require a requester to provide advance payment of an employee's compensation only for the time the employee is present during the requester's examination, not for pre-examination preparation, absent a judicial declaration allowing otherwise.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (opinion not withdrawn; statute text unchanged on this point through Acts 2024, No. 411)
resolutions.manual_verification: The categorical bar on search/retrieval labor charges is by statutory omission (only 'reasonable fees for making copies' are authorized) as construed by AG opinion and DOJ guidance, not by an express statutory prohibition; the AG framed the rule around examination requests and left a court free to authorize a fee. Confirm no post-2018 opinion or appellate decision permits search-time charges on copy requests.
resolutions.notes: Louisiana authorizes only 'reasonable fees for making copies' for local custodians; the AG's 'default rule' is that a requester may not be charged for 'a custodian's pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records' absent judicial authorization, and DOJ's 2023 guidance states 'Can't charge for the time to process the request' (LA-9012). Hence a search/retrieval hourly rate is not a lawful municipal parameter. Sole labor-like charge in the statute is 'reasonable compensation' for the custodian's representative during after-hours examination, funded in advance (LA-9007) — that is supervision of inspection, not search.

resolutions.source_language: No fee shall be charged to any person to examine or review any public records, except as provided in this Section, and no fee shall be charged for examination or review to determine if a record is subject to disclosure, except as may be determined by a court of competent jurisdiction.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)
resolutions.notes: 'No fee shall be charged for examination or review to determine if a record is subject to disclosure, except as may be determined by a court of competent jurisdiction' — review/redaction time is non-chargeable by statute unless a court sets a fee. AG Op. 17-0056 applies the same rule to copies made in the course of redaction (LA-9008). Judicial exception is a per-case court order, not a city parameter.

resolutions.source_language: If the court finds that the custodian arbitrarily or capriciously withheld the requested record or unreasonably or arbitrarily failed to respond to the request as required by R.S. 44:32, it may award the requestor any actual damages proven by him to have resulted from the actions of the custodian except as hereinafter provided.  In addition, if the court finds that the custodian unreasonably or arbitrarily failed to respond to the request as required by R.S. 44:32, it may award the requestor civil penalties not to exceed one hundred dollars per day, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays, for each such day of such failure to give notification.

new_rules.legal_concept: Commissioner of administration adopts uniform copy-fee schedule for executive-branch state agencies
new_rules.atomic_rule: The commissioner of administration, with the governor's approval, shall by rule adopt a uniform fee schedule for copies of public records of executive-branch state agencies, and such copies shall be furnished at the scheduled fees except where a fee is otherwise fixed by law.
new_rules.trigger: Request for copies of an executive-branch state agency's public records
new_rules.source_language: the commissioner of administration, with the approval of the governor, shall, by rule or regulation, adopt a uniform fee schedule for copies of public records of executive branch state agencies furnished to persons so requesting by custodians thereof, as provided by R.S. 44:32.  Copies of the public record furnished to a person so requesting shall be provided at fees according to the schedule, except for copies of public records, the fees for the reproduction of which are otherwise fixed by law.
new_rules.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY (executive branch). Delegation followed: 44:32(C)(2)(a) -> 39:241 -> LAC 4:I.301. Not binding on municipalities, whose fees rest on 44:32(C)(1)(a) (LA-0021).

new_rules.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: minimum $0.25 per page (paper/microfiche up to 8.5x14; two-sided = two pages)
new_rules.atomic_rule: For state agencies, charges for the first copy of any public record shall be at a minimum $0.25 per page for microfiche reproductions or paper copies up to 8 1/2 by 14 inches; a two-sided copy counts as two pages.
new_rules.trigger: State-agency copy request, paper/microfiche up to 8.5x14
new_rules.source_language: B.1. Charges for the first copy of any public records shall be at a minimum $0.25 per page for microfiche reproductions or paper copies up to 8 1/2 by 14 inches. 2. A two-sided copy shall be considered two pages.
new_rules.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(B)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Promulgated LR 8:411, Aug. 1982; amended LR 12:229, Apr. 1986; DOA compilation)
new_rules.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY; 'at a minimum' makes this a floor (an agency exceeding it must justify under §301.E, LA-9002/LA-9005). Cities are not bound; historically the AG urged local bodies to adopt this schedule 'to ensure objective reasonableness' (AG Op. 96-270 — not opened; cited second-hand, manual verification). Index page: https://www.doa.la.gov/doa/osr/louisiana-administrative-code/

new_rules.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: oversized copies at actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: For state agencies, charges for copies on paper larger than 8 1/2 by 14 inches shall equal the actual cost to the agency of copying them.
new_rules.trigger: State-agency copy request, paper larger than 8.5x14
new_rules.source_language: C. Charges for copies of public records on paper larger than 8 1/2 by 14 inches shall be the same as the actual cost to the agency for copying same.
new_rules.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(C)
new_rules.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. Standard term: 'actual cost to the agency'.

new_rules.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: computer-stored records — printout schedule approved by DOA; estimate required for programming; actual cost incl. programming charged if it differs
new_rules.atomic_rule: For state agencies, preprinted computer reports are charged at the §301 page rate; each agency shall adopt a DOA-approved schedule for database printouts; where reproduction requires program modification or specialized programs the requester shall be given an estimate, told it is an estimate, and charged the actual cost of reproduction including programming costs if it differs.
new_rules.trigger: State-agency request for computer-stored records requiring program modification or specialized programs
new_rules.source_language: D. Charges for copies of public records on preprinted computer reports shall be the same rate specified in §301.A and B. Each agency shall develop a uniform fee schedule for providing printouts of public records stored in a computer data base utilizing routing utility programs. Such uniform fee schedule shall be first approved by the Division of Administration. An estimated cost shall be given for reproduction of public records stored in a computer which require program modification or specialized programs. The requesting party shall be advised of the estimate, and that it is an estimate, but the actual cost for reproduction, including programming costs, shall be charged if it differs from the estimate.
new_rules.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(D)
new_rules.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. Bundles an estimate notice (structural), a programming-cost charge (actual cost), and an overrun rule (actual charged if it differs from estimate — no percentage trigger). Kept in one row because the source states them as one conditional sequence.

new_rules.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: agency fees above the schedule need written justification approved by DOA
new_rules.atomic_rule: A state agency with an established copy fee exceeding the schedule must justify that fee in writing and have it approved by the Division of Administration.
new_rules.trigger: State agency charges more than LAC 4:I.301 rates
new_rules.source_language: E. Agencies which have an established fee for copying public records that is in excess of those set forth in the rule must justify that fee in writing and have the established fee approved by the Division of Administration.
new_rules.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(E)
new_rules.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. §301.G: schedule does not apply where a fee is otherwise fixed by law nor to agency-to-agency requests: 'G. This schedule does not apply to copies of public records, the fees for the reproduction of which are otherwise fixed by law, nor shall this schedule apply to requests for copies from one state agency to another.'

new_rules.legal_concept: Uniform fee schedule: free or reduced copies for indigent citizens or public-purpose users
new_rules.atomic_rule: State agencies shall furnish copies without charge or at a reduced charge to indigent citizens of Louisiana or to persons whose use of the copies will be limited to a public purpose (e.g., a hearing before a governmental regulatory commission).
new_rules.trigger: State-agency requester is indigent or will use copies only for a public purpose
new_rules.source_language: F. Copies of public records shall be furnished without charge, or at a reduced charge, to indigent citizens of this state or the persons whose use of such copies will be limited to a public purpose, including, but not limited to, use in a hearing before any governmental regulatory commission.
new_rules.source_authority: La. Admin. Code tit. 4, pt. I, §301(F)
new_rules.notes: STATE AGENCIES ONLY. Note the rule says 'shall be furnished' whereas 44:32(C)(2)(a) says 'may be furnished' — statute governs (discretionary); the rule's mandatory phrasing is noted as an inconsistency. Municipal waiver ground is indigency only (LA-0025).

new_rules.legal_concept: Reasonable compensation for custodian's representative during after-hours examination, funded in advance by the examiner
new_rules.atomic_rule: Examinations must occur during regular office or working hours unless the custodian authorizes otherwise, in which event the persons designated to represent the custodian during the examination are entitled to reasonable compensation paid by the public body out of funds provided in advance by the person examining after hours.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian authorizes examination outside regular office/working hours
new_rules.source_language: examinations of records under the authority of this Section must be conducted during regular office or working hours, unless the custodian shall authorize examination of records in other than regular office or working hours.  In this event the persons designated to represent the custodian during such examination shall be entitled to reasonable compensation to be paid to them by the public body having custody of such record, out of funds provided in advance by the person examining such record in other than regular office or working hours.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (last amended Acts 2024, No. 411; fee text of (C)(1)(a) as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247, eff. Aug. 1, 2023; no 2025 or 2026 amendment found)
new_rules.notes: AMENDS LA-0027: source opened verbatim (is_paraphrase now false) and the citation corrected from 44:32(B) to 44:32(A)(1) (subsection B is the segregation clause). 'Reasonable compensation' is a soft standard the public body sets; AG 17-0056 (LA-9009) limits it to time the employee is present during the examination. Applies to all public bodies.

new_rules.legal_concept: No fee for retrieval, review, segregation/redaction time or for copies made in the course of redaction, absent judicial authorization
new_rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may not charge a requester for pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records, nor for copies the custodian makes in the process of redacting nonpublic information, unless a court authorizes such a fee; the only authorized fees are reasonable copy fees.
new_rules.trigger: Custodian incurs staff time locating, reviewing, or redacting records
new_rules.source_language: You ask whether the official can be paid for the time spent retrieving the responsive documents, and more specifically, the time spent segregating public and non-public records. As outlined above, La. R.S. 44:32(B) states that if a record contains material which is not public, the non-public information may be segregated from the response; however, La. R.S. 44:32 does not specifically authorize a fee to be collected in this scenario. If such segregation takes an extraordinary amount of time to compile, then the elected official may wish to consult with the city attorney to determine whether it is appropriate for the city to seek a judicial determination requesting that a fee be charged to the requestor for the segregation. [quoted from a prior opinion] ... Thus, although the law allows a custodian to collect reasonable fees when a request seeks copies of public records, there is no specific authorization for a fee to be collected for segregating or redacting nonpublic information when a request seeks only to inspect public records. As such, we are of the opinion that the general rule of La. R.S. 44:32(C)(3) applies when a public records custodian makes copies of public records in the process of redacting nonpublic information when responding to a request to examine public records, and a custodian may not charge a fee to the requester for such copies unless the custodian receives judicial authorization for such a fee.
new_rules.source_authority: La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 17-0056 (Apr. 2, 2018), pp. 5-7, construing La. R.S. 44:32(B), (C)(1)-(3)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (opinion issued Apr. 2, 2018; clarified on other points by Op. 17-0056A, July 27, 2018)
new_rules.notes: Text extracted by OCR from the AG's scanned PDF; wording checked against the page image. Opinion addressed a parish sheriff (local body) — treated as applying to all custodians. The prior opinion it quotes is printed as 'La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0173'; the opinion posted under that number on the AG portal is unrelated (vessel salvage), so the quoted opinion's number needs manual verification. Framed mainly around inspection requests; DOJ's 2023 guidance (LA-9012) states the rule generally: 'Can't charge for the time to process the request.'

new_rules.legal_concept: After-hours compensation limited to time the employee is present during the examination, not preparation
new_rules.atomic_rule: A custodian may require advance payment of an employee's compensation only for the time the employee is present during the requester's after-hours examination, not for pre-examination preparation, absent a judicial declaration allowing otherwise.
new_rules.trigger: After-hours examination authorized; custodian seeks compensation for preparation/overtime
new_rules.source_language: No provision of the Public Records Law directly authorizes such a charge to the requester. We must therefore return to La. R.S. 44:32(C)(3) and the default rule that a requester may not be charged a fee in connection with a request to examine public records, nor for a custodian's pre-examination retrieval, review, and separation of records. See La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0173, supra. We are therefore of the opinion that a custodian may require a requester to provide advance payment of an employee's compensation only for the time the employee is present during the requester's examination, not for pre-examination preparation, absent a judicial declaration allowing otherwise.
new_rules.source_authority: La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 17-0056 (Apr. 2, 2018), p. 7
new_rules.notes: OCR-extracted verbatim. Same opinion reaffirms that after-hours inspection may be required only when the request 'disrupts normal office procedure to the point where the office ceases to operate' (citing Ops. 96-0079, 98-0366, 01-0244).

new_rules.legal_concept: 'Reasonable fee' for copies includes at minimum the actual cost of making the copies; excludes generation cost/value of the information
new_rules.atomic_rule: A reasonable copy fee under 44:32(C)(1)(a) is fact-specific, is not designed to recoup the cost of preparing the records, does not include the original cost of generating the information or its value, and includes at a minimum the actual costs for making the copies.
new_rules.trigger: Non-state-agency custodian sets or applies a copy fee (incl. electronic copy on disc)
new_rules.source_language: The Public Records Act allows a custodian to charge a "reasonable fee" for making copies of public records. What constitutes a reasonable fee is ultimately a fact-specific question. However, we do note that the Public Records Act is not designed to recoup costs incurred by a public entity in preparing the records requested. Similar to the scenario you have presented, though, when considering what constituted a reasonable fee for providing access to an electronic copy of the assessment rolls, the First Circuit Court of Appeals stated: "This fee does not include the original cost of generation of the information or the actual value of the information. It does include, at a minimum, the actual costs for making the copies."
new_rules.source_authority: La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0056 (Oct. 8, 2015), p. 4 (quoting Granger v. Litchfield, 94-0114 (La. App. 1 Cir. 11/10/94), 645 So.2d 1262)
new_rules.notes: Text-layer PDF, opened. Opinion addressed a parish assessor (local body); footnote 7 confirms 44:32(C)(1)(a) governs non-state agencies. Gives the reasonableness standard content without a number.

new_rules.legal_concept: No per-page fee when a requester copies records with a personal hand-held scanner during inspection
new_rules.atomic_rule: A person who inspects public records and copies them with a personal hand-held scanner is not obligated to pay a per-page fee.
new_rules.trigger: Requester makes own copies with own equipment during inspection
new_rules.source_language: a person who makes a valid public records request to inspect documents and at the time of inspection uses a personal hand-held scanner to copy said public records is not obligated to pay a fee for each page copied.
new_rules.notes: OCR-extracted verbatim; scanned PDF. Relies on Title Research Corp. v. Rausch, 450 So.2d 933 (La. 1984); Thornton v. DPS, 536 So.2d 595 (La. App. 1 Cir. 1988); Alliance for Affordable Energy v. Frick, 695 So.2d 1126 (La. App. 4 Cir. 1997); First Commerce Title v. Martin, 887 So.2d 716 (La. App. 2 Cir. 2004). Footnote 2: the only fees chargeable to a person merely inspecting are after-hours supervision (44:32(A)) and a court-set fee for pre-disclosure review (44:32(C)(3)).

new_rules.legal_concept: DOJ guidance: no charge for time to process a request; charge only for copying and electronic transmission; posted schedule required
new_rules.atomic_rule: Per Louisiana DOJ guidance, a custodian cannot charge for the time to process a request, to examine/review records, or for a requester's own scanner; a custodian can charge for copying (state agencies per the Administrative Code, non-state agencies a reasonable fee) and for transmission of electronic copies, and must post a fee schedule.
new_rules.source_language: Fees (44:32) • Providing public records is a duty and service you offer • Can't charge for the time to process the request • Can't charge people to examine or review records • Can't charge someone for bringing their own scanner • CAN charge for copying • State agencies (Administrative Code) • Non-state agencies (reasonable) • CAN charge for the transmission of electronic copies of public records (non-state agencies) • **Need fee schedule posted (Acts 2023, No. 247) • Timing of payment
new_rules.source_authority: Louisiana Department of Justice, 'Public Records Law' (Alicia Edmond Wheeler, Asst. Attorney General), 2023 CLE outline, slide 'Fees (44:32)', p. 21
new_rules.notes: Official guidance, not law — ranks below statute and formal AG opinions; included because it states the labor rule generally (not limited to inspection requests). Slide bullets reproduced verbatim; separator '•' added between bullets.

new_rules.legal_concept: Reasonable copy fee may include transmission of electronic copies
new_rules.atomic_rule: The custodian's reasonable copy fee may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
new_rules.trigger: Requester asks for electronic copies / electronic delivery
new_rules.source_language: The custodian may establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, which may include the transmission of electronic copies of public records.
new_rules.source_authority: La. R.S. 44:32(C)(1)(a) (as amended by Acts 2023, No. 247 (SB 213), eff. Aug. 1, 2023)
new_rules.notes: Split from LA-0021 so electronic-copy/transmission charges join the fee.electronic_media_charge / delivery concepts. Act 247 résumé digest: 'Existing law allows a custodian ... to establish and collect reasonable fees for making copies of public records, including the transmission of electronic copies ... New law ... further requires a custodian of public records that are not public records of a state agency who elects to establish and collect fees under existing law to set and publicly post a reasonable fee schedule.' Non-state-agency custodians (municipalities).

delegations_followed.instrument_cite: n/a — municipal instrument, not a state instrument

delegations_followed.figures_extracted: none — judicial exception to the no-fee-for-review rule is case-by-case

applicability_notes: Louisiana runs two fee regimes: 44:32(C)(1)(a) for 'all public records, except public records of state agencies' (municipalities, parishes, sheriffs, school boards, etc.: 'reasonable fees for making copies', posted schedule) and 44:32(C)(2)(a) for state agencies (uniform schedule under R.S. 39:241 -> LAC 4:I.301, $0.25/page minimum). Every LAC 4:I.301 figure in this file is state_agencies_only; municipal items resolve to the reasonable-fee soft standard.

LAC 4:I.401/§403 (Department of State: $0.25/page paper, CD/USB, e-mail; $20 certification; postage actual; credit card/check/money order) are agency-specific schedules of one department — cited only as examples, never as municipal values.

The labor prohibition (no charge for retrieval/review/redaction time) is express in statute only for examination/review time (44:32(C)(3)); its extension to search time on copy requests is the AG's construction (Op. 17-0056; DOJ 2023 CLE). Recorded as applying to all custodians, confidence medium.
44:32(C)(2)(b) (free copies to student media of public postsecondary institutions, Acts 2024, No. 411) and the 'public purpose' waiver ground (44:32(C)(2)(a)) do not apply to municipalities.
44:32(C)(1)(b)-(c) (clerks of court / Orleans recorders may adopt uniform reproduction procedures; no private copying equipment in clerk offices) are custodian-specific and not municipal.
material_negatives: No statutory per-page copy rate, cap, minimum, free-page allowance, graduated bands, or de-minimis for municipalities — only 'reasonable fees for making copies' plus a mandatory posted schedule (44:32(C)(1)(a)).
No labor/search/programming rates and no chargeable-labor threshold; staff time is non-chargeable per 44:32(C)(3) and AG construction, with a court-order exception only.

No estimate threshold, itemization requirement, requester response window, estimate validity period, revision percentage, or overrun re-issue rule for local bodies (advance notice of the amount is required before the nonpayment excuse applies).
No deposit threshold or percentage cap; advance payment permitted without limit; no clock effect stated while payment is pending.
No electronic-payment mandate, certification fee, audio/video pricing, commercial-purpose schedule, fee forfeiture on late response, or request-aggregation rule.
2026 RS SB 493, which would have created a 20-page free allowance and 5c/page ceiling for non-state agencies, was withdrawn — the prior figures floating in secondary sources are NOT law.
gaps_manual_verification: AG Op. 96-270 (recommending local adoption of the $0.25 state schedule) — cited by RCFP/secondary sources; AG portal download returned empty. Verify text and whether it is still cited by the AG.

AG Op. 17-0056 quotes an earlier opinion printed as 'La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 15-0173'; the opinion at that number on the AG portal concerns vessel salvage — the quoted opinion's true number needs verification.

AG opinions 17-0056, 17-0044 were extracted by OCR from scanned PDFs; wording was checked against page images for the quoted passages but should be re-read by a human before entering the library as verbatim.

Programming/data-extraction charges for local bodies (labor.programming.rate) sit between AG 15-0056 ('actual costs for making the copies') and DOJ guidance ('Can't charge for the time to process the request') — needs a human call or a later AG opinion.
Whether continued withholding for unpaid fees interacts with the 44:32(D)/44:35(A) five-day and 44:33(B) three-day clocks is unaddressed by statute (payment.depositClock).

Custodian-specific certified-copy and record-type fee statutes outside Title 44 (clerks of court, vital records, accident reports, body-camera footage) were not inventoried; confirm none binds municipal police/clerk custodians generally.

LAC 4:I.301's edition date: DOA compilation file '04v01-09.docx' carries no as-of date in its text; the historical note (LR 12:229, Apr. 1986) was the last amendment shown — confirm no 2024–2026 Louisiana Register amendment.
